why_points: The pick: Rec yds lower 8.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 4.5, moved to this line) is 61%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 6.5. This is the best number for the lower side.
Game log, most recent first: 5, 0, 0, 34, 23, 13. Weighted average 10.4; went lower than 8.5 in 3 of 6 games (63% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 1.7 vs 23.3 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±12.3, so the line is 0.2 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — basically a coin flip.
Matchup: LAC is about league-average against TEs.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +4% on his average.

PFF: LAC allows 1.52 yds/route to TEs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.45) → +3% against his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 12.1 receiving yards on average; in a typical game 7.7 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.8 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 50% and the matchup 51%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 59%, matchup 59%.
Bottom line: we give it 59% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +2.8 points; that works out to about +5¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
